title: AML Agents Briefing — Thursday, 30 July 2026
script:
ALEX: Welcome to AML Agents Briefing. It's Wednesday the thirtieth of July 2026, and this is your audio overview of the most material AML and financial crime developments across the Asia-Pacific region today. Full detail, the obligation register, and horizon scanning are all at amlagents dot streamlit dot app.

JORDAN: Big day, Alex. We've got a structural shift in fintech licensing, an AI spend-management story with real trade-finance implications, and some forward-looking items that AUSTRAC-regulated firms genuinely cannot afford to miss.

ALEX: Let's get into it. The story I want to lead with today is Increase, the banking infrastructure fintech founded by Stripe's first employee. The firm has acquired an undisclosed community bank in the United States, which moves it from being a middleware provider sitting on top of licensed institutions, to owning the depository licence itself.

JORDAN: Why does that matter for our listeners, most of whom are sitting in Singapore, Hong Kong, or Sydney?

ALEX: Because the compliance architecture changes entirely when you own the charter. As a middleware firm, Increase's AML obligations flowed through its bank partners. Now it becomes the regulated entity. It sets its own customer due diligence standards, files its own suspicious activity reports, and faces direct supervisory scrutiny. The analogy in this region would be a payment service provider acquiring a locally incorporated bank rather than operating under a principal arrangement.

JORDAN: Right, and for MLROs at fintechs in this region who are currently operating under a principal bank's AML programme, this is actually a useful prompt. If your growth trajectory means you're likely to apply for your own full banking licence, or if a group restructuring brings a licensed entity under your umbrella, your compliance perimeter expands materially overnight. The action here is to get your AML programme gap analysis done before the structural change, not after. Map what your bank partner currently owns, what you would need to own, and where your transaction monitoring coverage has gaps.

ALEX: Moving on, Freehand has raised seventy-five million US dollars for AI agents that autonomously manage supply chain expenditure. Their clients include Meta and Pfizer. This is a category of software that sits directly in the trade-based money laundering risk space.

JORDAN: So what should compliance leaders take from this?

ALEX: The risk is that autonomous AI agents making procurement and payment decisions on behalf of corporates become a new layer of opacity in trade flows. If the AI is routing payments, approving invoices, and managing supplier relationships without human review at each step, the traditional correspondent banking checks and the trade finance due diligence frameworks are working against an intermediary that doesn't look like a traditional intermediary.

JORDAN: And for heads of trade finance compliance or financial crime risk at banks with correspondent relationships into the United States or European supply chains, the read-across is this. Start asking your corporate clients whether they are deploying AI spend-management platforms, and if so, who retains ultimate payment authorisation. Your know-your-customer programme was designed around human decision-makers. Update your customer risk assessment templates to capture AI-mediated payment flows, because FATF Recommendation 16 on wire transfers still applies regardless of whether a human or an algorithm initiated the instruction.

ALEX: Shifting our focus, Jordan, over to you on the Temenos story.

JORDAN: Yes, so Temenos has appointed Cormac Flanagan as Chief Product Officer and Tony Coleman as Chief Technology Officer, both effective the third of August. Temenos's core banking platform underpins transaction monitoring and compliance workflows at a significant number of institutions across this region, particularly in Singapore and Southeast Asia.

ALEX: The read-across for me is vendor governance. When a core platform vendor makes senior leadership changes at the product and technology level simultaneously, it's a signal that the product roadmap may shift. For MLROs relying on Temenos-hosted or Temenos-integrated transaction monitoring, this is the moment to get clarity from your vendor relationship manager on what, if anything, changes in the compliance module development pipeline.

JORDAN: Exactly. Add a standing item to your next vendor review meeting. Ask specifically about the AML and financial crime product roadmap under the new leadership, and confirm your current integration commitments are still on schedule. Do not wait for the annual review.

ALEX: Before we close, what to watch. Three items on the horizon that listeners should be actioning this week.

JORDAN: The first is for AUSTRAC-regulated firms. There is a forty-seven million Australian dollar civil penalty against a major digital currency exchange for systemic failures in transaction monitoring, mule-account detection, and suspicious matter report timeliness. If you are a digital currency exchange registered with AUSTRAC, pull your SMR timeliness metrics today. Regulators have now shown they will pursue large penalties for systemic failure, not just individual missed filings.

JORDAN: The second is the AUSTRAC Tranche 2 guidance for legal practitioners. If your institution onboards law firms as clients, review that guidance now. It tells you what AUSTRAC expects those firms to be doing on source-of-wealth diligence in conveyancing, which in turn tells you what your correspondent and business-banking due diligence should be asking.

JORDAN: The third is the Bank Negara Malaysia typology bulletin on investment scams and money mules routed through digital banks and crypto exchanges. If you are running a digital bank or an e-money institution in Malaysia, cross-reference those mule-account indicators, specifically rapid post-onboarding velocity spikes and inbound flows from multiple unrelated retail senders, against your current transaction monitoring rules. If your scenarios do not capture that pattern, escalate to your monitoring team before the end of this week.

JORDAN: Full detail on all of today's stories, the obligation register, and horizon scanning is at amlagents dot streamlit dot app.

ALEX: Thanks for listening. We'll be back tomorrow with the next briefing. Stay sharp.
